origin: Codex research directed by repository owner

claims.statement: Equations (1)-(3) give all Koszul ranks of convolutions, in all leg orientations and with a padded shared space, over C.
claims.limitations: Standard constructions rederived here; no historical priority claim. Not a complete degeneration criterion.

claims.statement: k copies of C(a,b) sharing their full output space with arbitrary invertible identifications and disjoint input spaces have rank and border rank k(a+b-1).
claims.limitations: Does not assert border-rank additivity for arbitrary shared-leg sums.

claims.statement: All 85 specific candidate packings in the archived dimension search violate a Koszul-rank inequality; 180 oriented and 27 padded direct matrix checks agree with the formulas.
claims.limitations: Alternative packings are not exhausted. The general rank formulas rely on the written proofs.

claims.statement: The canonical mixed family passes all full-space Koszul tests on all three legs for every k>=1; its P_* score surplus is (4k-210)/81.
claims.limitations: Source degeneration unconstructed; projected and other Young flattenings not covered; no exponent implication established.

claims.statement: The canonical four-block target T has border rank 10 via ten-point triangular-grid interpolation; T tensor B_X(k) has border rank 10k.
claims.limitations: Certificate starts from a diagonal tensor, not from C(4,10k); no priority claim for the interpolation construction.

claims.statement: Coordinate selection, rescaling and diagonal weights realizing the four-type target from C(4,B) require B>=12k-1.
claims.limitations: Arbitrary linear changes of basis are excluded from this obstruction.

claims.statement: For every actual tensor character at t=3/4, the rescaled symmetrized convolution profile has the forced homogeneous form, without a C1 assumption.
dependencies: UZ26 v2 Lemma 4.1 and Appendix F
claims.limitations: Does not construct or exclude a critical character. External rescaling theorem is imported, not re-formalized.

claims.statement: A uniform positive normalized curvature delta0 for actual characters with t>=t0<3/4 implies omega<=max(3t0,9/(4(1+delta0))).
claims.limitations: The positive curvature premise remains unproved.

claims.statement: Massarenti-Raviolo Remark 3.3 excludes exact-rank schemes beating 9/4 at n=34..37; at n=38 only rank 3585 survives the two bounds used.
claims.limitations: External exact-rank premise; not a border-rank bound or an exhaustive literature frontier.

claims.statement: For every m>=2 and k>=1, the canonical mixed target has border rank k*m*(m+1)/2 and passes every full-space Koszul test against C(m,k*m*(m+1)/2).
claims.limitations: No source degeneration or general projected/Young-flattening criterion is supplied.

claims.statement: The specified coordinate-weight ansatz requires B>=k*m*(m+1)/2+k*floor((m-1)^2/4)-floor((m-1)/2), asymptotically 50 percent overhead.
claims.limitations: Arbitrary linear changes of basis and coordinate collisions are outside the ansatz.

claims.statement: An unbounded sequence of the specified convolution degenerations with asymptotic overhead below 9/(7*cuberoot(2))-1 implies omega<9/4; zero overhead implies omega<=125/56.
claims.limitations: The source-degeneration premise H(rho) is unproved; no new exponent is established.
claims.attribution: The stronger limiting-slope estimate is adopted from concurrent commit cf79709; this note verifies it for the single joint-sequence H(rho) premise.

claims.statement: Any ordinary linear restriction C(m,B) to the canonical T_(m,k) requires B>=k*m*m-m+1, asymptotically 100 percent overhead.
claims.limitations: The rank argument does not extend to arbitrary polynomial degenerations.
claims.attribution: Strengthened using the minimum-slice argument of concurrent commit d2d505c; the previous maximum-slice bound gave 50 percent overhead.

claims.statement: The catalecticant obstruction extends the coordinate overhead bound to arbitrary polynomial Y/Z changes when the shared X coefficient structure is fixed or transformed by its binary-form GL(2) action.
claims.limitations: General GL(m) changes of the shared factor are outside the scope.

claims.statement: Explicit coordinate degenerations prove the m=2 all-k and m=3,k=1 positive controls; 32 bounded real/complex m=4 fits produced no certificate.
claims.limitations: Numerical failures are not orbit-closure exclusions; fixed-m controls do not meet H(rho).

claims.statement: If L(v(z)) has its global maximum rank r on the coefficient rational normal curve, the source C(m,B) flattening has rank at least Br; every border-rank-B target has rank at most Br. This includes all projected shared Koszul and linear equivariant shared Young/Pieri maps of the stated form.
claims.limitations: Other-factor and nonlinear invariants are not exhausted; the curve-rank hypothesis is essential and fails for the structured catalecticant obstruction.

claims.statement: For degree-ordered shared coordinates, coordinate selection/rescaling/diagonal-weight degenerations in any degree-graded orthogonal polynomial basis require asymptotically at least 50 percent overhead for the canonical all-degree target.
claims.limitations: Arbitrary shared permutations and general linear combinations are outside this all-size statement.

claims.statement: For every m=4,...,38, each nonidentity shared Chebyshev ordering with degree zero first admits at most one center for a C(2,m-1) block. The written reduction excludes that coordinate construction of T_(m,k) at low overhead for all k and admissible B at these m.
claims.limitations: Not an all-size center-uniqueness theorem. Discovery at m=39 timed out. Reduction and code remain subject to independent review. Small normalized controls are not exponent improvements.

claims.statement: The catalecticant cost bound holds for arbitrary constant invertible shared bases, and regular shared maps with invertible limit, even with independently rotated target sectors. Its asymptotic overhead is 50 percent.
claims.limitations: Genuinely singular shared maps remain outside the proof. The biform dimension lemma is not a new exponent bound.
dependencies: Standard projective dimension theorem, Stacks Project tag 0B2R

claims.statement: The structured flattening lower bound extends from convolution blocks to every bilinear block with no zero divisors and dimensions (j+1,m-j,m). The matched all-degree family still requires asymptotic 50 percent overhead with constant shared basis.
claims.limitations: This is a construction-class obstruction, not a border-rank lower bound or an exponent improvement.

claims.statement: For constant P,Q,G followed by the specified monomial degree weights, alpha>(m-1)*abs(beta) has the catalecticant cost obstruction; 0<alpha<=beta requires B>=k*(2N-floor(m^2/4)-1)-(m-1).
claims.limitations: Intermediate slopes and arbitrary parameter-dependent shared maps remain open. Ten retained floating runs are diagnostics in the now-excluded dominant-degree class, not certificates.

claims.statement: Exact slice covers give asymptotic source ratio at least 2-r/2 when alpha/beta tends to r in [1,2]. The balanced (2,1) direction requires B>=k*(N+floor(m/2))-(m-1), excluding m=4,B=10k for k>=2.
claims.limitations: Constant P,Q,G followed by the specified weights only. The single-copy balanced m=4 case, its growing-m analogue, larger intermediate slopes and general Laurent maps are not excluded. No exponent improvement is established.

claims.statement: Existing tripling and two-sector constructions imply 6P(a,a)<=(6a-2)^(1/t). Either the stated universal near-endpoint lower bound P(4,4)>=5005/486, or a degeneration of the product of all six leg permutations of C(4,4) to M(106,106,106), implies omega<=2249/1000 with exact integer certificates.
claims.limitations: The new universal profile lower bound is unproved and the M(106,106,106) degeneration is unconstructed. The displayed smaller exponent is conditional and not established.
claims.attribution: Combines OpenAI's shifted tripling and detection with the concurrent two-sector construction at f6f307c.

claims.statement: At an endpoint character, extracting independent matrix products from any power of the fully symmetrized C(a,a) can force a profile lower bound no greater than sqrt(a*a*(2a-1)). This cannot cross the finite endpoint ceiling for a=1,2,3; a=4 is the first diagonal not excluded by the screen.
claims.limitations: Only this source and direct-sum matrix targets without extra source tensors are covered. No surviving extraction or exponent improvement is constructed.

claims.statement: Eleven nonaffine shared permutations at m=4,B=10,direction (5,2) completed 600-evaluation fits each. No exact witness was obtained; saved full-tensor diagnostics do not show a small tensor error.
claims.limitations: Floating fits and sampled epsilon errors are neither exact certificates nor impossibility proofs.

claims.statement: For powers of the fully symmetrized C(a,a), coordinate injections and diagonal weights into independent matrix products can force a profile lower bound no greater than (a^8*(2a-1)^5)^(1/9). At a=4 this is below the finite endpoint ceiling, excluding that route at every power; a single square target is at most M49.
claims.limitations: General linear combinations and cancellations are not covered. This is a limitation on the extraction method, not an upper bound on the actual character profile or an exponent result.
claims.attribution: Applies the abelian opposite-relation argument of concurrent dcfc1ef, with explicit label factorization, group embedding, and Holder dimension accounting.

claims.statement: Explicit invertible diagonal scaling gives uniform marginals for every complex C(a,b). Every singleton quantum functional has value V_a^2 on the six-permutation product S_a and n^2 on M(n,n,n), so this whole family permits the H106 finite target.
claims.limitations: These spectral points need not exhaust the spectrum; their necessary inequalities do not construct a degeneration.
claims.attribution: Uses Christandl-Vrana-Zuiddam arXiv:1709.07851v3 Definition 3.16 and Theorem 3.30; elementary binomial normalization rederived with no priority claim.

claims.statement: Every diagonal-weight coordinate extraction of independent matrix products from S_a^q has endpoint profile-certificate ceiling (a^8*(2a-1)^5)^(1/9)*exp(-2/[81*(2a-1)^2]). This is below the finite critical ceiling also at a=5, for all powers q.
claims.limitations: A ceiling on this extraction method, not on actual character values. Does not exclude general linear input mixing or arbitrary Laurent maps, and the stated finite comparison does not close all a>=6.
claims.attribution: Extends the adopted abelian opposite-relation bound from concurrent dcfc1ef using integer potential widths and an elementary entropy deficit.

claims.statement: For a coordinate restriction of an abelian group tensor G with third-leg dimension d, coordinate injections with nonzero Laurent scalars on the first two legs and arbitrary Laurent output can degenerate to M(l,h,n) only if h*(3*l*n-2*d)<=|G|. For S_4 this forces square targets n<=93 and excludes H106 in that class.
claims.limitations: Neither a construction of M93 nor an obstruction to arbitrary mixing of input coordinates. Written proof remains unreviewed.
claims.attribution: Adopts the Laurent active-set disjointness lemma merged at 7d97155 and the abelian opposite-relation lemma at dcfc1ef; adds the dense singleton-component argument.
